title: Physical shape of a rule package version and of the model answer is not specified
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 15 (what is stored for every version); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owned by P7, and the path GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md T3.1
section: 11. Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: No source gives the physical column names of rule_package_version (state, valid-from date, approver, workbook, generated DRL, SHA-256) or the response body in which GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} returns the compiled model to an owning service. Slide 15 fixes what a version stores and the Ownership Map fixes the owner of the tables and of the path, but neither gives a physical definition or a payload schema, and TSD P7 T3.1 defines only decision_log_entry and approval.
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design slide 15 lists the stored items of a rule_package_version as the workbook in Blob, the generated DRL, the SHA-256, the valid-from date and the approver, with no physical types or names; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 name GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} without a response shape; ownership.json rows rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case carry an owner and a ruling and no fields; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 has decision_log_entry and approval only.
proposed: Add the rule_package_version columns and the model answer of GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} (package code, version label, SHA-256, state, valid-from date, approver and an opaque artifact reference) to the rwb_decision physical schema and to the OpenAPI document of this service before wave 1 exit.

title: Two sources name different rule IDs for the same MORTGAGE in BKK allocation
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md A2.2, A2.3, A2.4, A2.5 and A2.8 (AC-P7-002-01 and the same wording repeated); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slide 16 and its notes; FSD P3 AC-P3-007 and legacy RWB-E1-020 AC1
section: 1. Story; 7. Acceptance criteria (AC1); 8. Business rules (BR2); 18. Traceability
description: The FSD P7 main success flow records the case as given to owner U-7101 by row ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01 of ALLOC-2026.11, while the Temporal and Drools design, FSD P3 AC-P3-007 and the legacy story record the same MORTGAGE in BKK allocation as ALLOC-014 with queue MTG-BKK-CO and owner U-03. Two different rule IDs describe one rule, so the value carried on the decision entry and asserted in the tests is not fixed by the sources.
evidence: FSD P7 A2.2 AC-P7-002-01: given owner U-7101 by row ALLOC-MTG-BKK-01 of ALLOC-2026.11 in JOB-03. Temporal and Drools slide 16: row ALLOC-014 for MORTGAGE in BKK to queue MTG-BKK-CO, with owners U-01, U-02 and U-03 at 120, 95 and 140 and U-03 chosen. Legacy RWB-E1-020 AC1 and AC2 use ALLOC-014 and U-03.
owner_role: Business analyst P7 with the service owner of rwb-decision
proposed: Correct the FSD P7 worked example to ALLOC-014, MTG-BKK-CO and U-03 so that the sample in the functional specification matches the decision table and the story; until then the Temporal and Drools design wins under R-PREC and ALLOC-014 is the value carried.

title: DecisionRecorded payload for an allocation carries no fixed business date or actions field names
source: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON envelope (rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md T3.1 (DF-DEC-031 idempotency_key, DF-DEC-014 actions); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 row 08 and slide 28; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03
description: The story records one allocation per case and business date, and the actions payload carries the assignment rule ID and version with the queue and owner identifiers. No source fixes how the business date an entry is keyed on travels in the DecisionRecorded envelope, which service stamps it, or what the actions payload calls the queue and owner values: TSD P7 T3.1 gives the columns and not their content, and the idempotency rule of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is stated for a record key and not for this event's fields.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists decision_log_entry.idempotency_key as varchar(80) with no format, and actions as jsonb with no field list; Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 gives DecisionRecorded as produced by all 19 services with no payload; Arch v5 slide 28 and FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-03 fix one entry per repeated event but not the business date; no source names the queue and owner keys of an allocation record.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-case with the platform library owner of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON
proposed: Publish the business date field on the DecisionRecorded envelope and the actions keys for the queue and owner identifiers in RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before wave 1 exit, with rwb-case stamping the business date it allocated for.
